pr_title: network: make GRE and GRETAP support Key= or friends
pr_comments: @ssahani Thank you for the comments. I've renamed the variable and functions. PTAL.

issue_context.title: systemd-networkd complete passing tunnel options
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently the netdev [Tunnel] options have `Key=`, `InputKey=` and `OutputKey=` parameters that were originally added for VTI/VTI6 tunnels, but are just as applicable to any GRE variant. In fact ERSPAN already does use those even though the documentation has not been updated reflect that fact.

ERSPAN also added `SerializeTunneledPackets=` that is also applicable to all GRE variants as well.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
As far as I understand the exact parameter passing logic for `key`, `ikey`, `okey` and `erspan_sequence` as is now in `netdev_erspan_fill_message_create` (src/network/netdev/tunnel.c) can be coped to `netdev_ip6gre_fill_message_create` and `netdev_gre_fill_message_create` as is.

The only issue would be the somewhat unfortunate variable naming with `erspan_sequence` and code repetition.

Sync the documentation. At the very least to reflect that ERSPAN can already use the Key*= parameters (not just VTI/VTI6).

That looks quite good. A lot better than the stuff I had briefly experimented to get my use case to work, but I wasn't happy with the redundant code, lack of tests and also wanted to look better into iproute2 over the weekend.

I think this closes the `Key*=` and `SerializeTunneledPackets=` perfectly and solves my original use case/problem.

But there are still cases of iproute2 offering much more control, but many of them are not as trivial (need new parameters).

A incomplete list (mostly GRE tunnels) that I had scribbled:

* There is the `AllowLocalRemote=` that is also offered as a gre option (`[no]allow-localremote`) via iproute2, never used it so I'm not sure if this is a generic or situational option.
* There is the `[i|o]csum` (`GRE_CSUM`) although it's usefulness is maybe debatable it should definitively be applicable to all to GRE variants.
* `FooOverUDP=` only appears to be usable with IPIP even though it can be used with GRE/SIT tunnels (`TUNNEL_ENCAP_FOU`). Not reflected in documentation.
* `gue` (Generic UDP Encapsulation) is not offered at all?
* Fragmentation control via (`[no]ignore-df`) `IFLA_GRE_IGNORE_DF`

And so on (haven't completely researched this), but should this be in an another issue or?
